static_traits.name: Yang Russell
static_traits.social_status: Staying in touch with friends who share the same interests, but Relationship tension due to feelings of self-insufficiency and comparison; not yet expressing disappointment and frustration to others.
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before; has not received psychotherapy; no major physical illness.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperation, positive attitude; able to identify and describe his/her 'should' thoughts; tends toward self-criticism; steady tone, coherent thinking.

basic_info.main_problem: Long-term disappointment and frustration from not yet becoming a professional Skateboarder; frequently Demands himself with 'should' statements and compares himself with successful skaters, leading to increased psychological stress and diminished enjoyment of skateboarding.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize this disappointment and constant comparison have affected my mental health and my enjoyment of skateboarding, which prompted me to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: A few years ago, due to financial constraints and lack of support, had to give up the dream of pursuing professional skateboarding; since then, whenever seeing skateboarding-related content or successful skaters, strong self-comparison and Sense of frustration are triggered, and the problem has gradually worsened.

core_beliefs: I failed (it is already too late)

special_situations.event: Seeing content of successful professional Skateboarders on social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am still not a professional skater now, it means I am not good enough / a failure.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting unrealistic goals and forcing myself to train harder, trying to catch up with others.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should already be a professional skater; I should be as good as them.

special_situations.event: When trying to participate in skateboard practice or competitions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach professional level, I have no right to enjoy skateboarding or be recognized.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcing myself to train extra with harsh self-talk, trying to eliminate unease by working harder.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have failed; it is already too late.

special_situations.event: When spending time with successful skater friends or talking about Career development
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not as good as them, it proves I am not good enough and not worthy of respect.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing communication, not talking about my disappointment, to avoid being compared or judged.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them.

special_situations.event: Recalling giving up the professional dream back then due to insufficient finances and support
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I had not persisted to the end or received enough support back then, it means the failure is entirely my fault.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly blaming myself, thinking I should have worked harder or done things differently back then.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have worked harder back then, otherwise I would not have failed.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to gain recognition and self-worth by becoming a professional Skateboarder, and to find lasting joy and meaning in skateboarding.
core_conflict.fear: Fearing appearing inferior after comparison and being seen as a failure; fearing the opportunity is already missed and never being able to realize the dream.
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control and self-esteem through strict self-demands and 'should' rules
Avoiding expressing vulnerability to friends to reduce the risk of shame and being judged

object_relations.object_representation: Others (successful skaters/friends) are judges and superiors

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing successful skaters or being asked about career achievement and level
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing others' success as negation of oneself, reinforcing the inner belief 'I am a failure' (transference: turning pressure and aggression toward the self).
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Respond in a gentle, Empathy tone, avoiding comparison or evaluation; use open-ended questions to invite description of current feelings and needs, validate the experience, and encourage rewriting self-criticism as expressions of feelings and wishes.

manifestations: Enjoyment of skateboarding declines after giving up career dreams
Frequently comparing with successful people, triggering disappointment and self-deprecation
Unable to continue professional pursuit due to financial constraints and lack of support, feeling Restricted choices
Not yet having talked to anyone about my disappointment and frustration
Relationship tension with successful skater friends

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using statements such as 'I should already be a professional skater''I should be as good as that person'
Measures self-worth by outside achievement standards

contact_model.definition: The individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not yet expressing disappointment and stress to friends or others
Turns frustration into self-blame and self-attack

positive_force: Has strong passion for skateboarding and willingness for long-term commitment
Has some self-awareness, able to identify and willing to adjust 'should' thoughts
Has friends with similar interests and community resources (though not yet well utilized)
Open attitude toward change, willing to try recording and restructuring thoughts
negative_force: Rigid 'should' rules and external achievement standards
Excessive comparison and Self-denial, easily overlooking positive experiences
Self-blame; believes oneself a failure and 'too late'
Setting unrealistic goals and applying excessive pressure
Insufficient finances and support leading to Limited opportunities

target_behavior.behavior: When in contact with skateboarding-related content or interacting with successful skateboarders, strong self-comparison and self-criticism appear
antecedent: Browsing skateboarding content on social media
Actually participating in skateboarding practice or competitions
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized rigid external achievement standards ('should' rules) and the core belief 'I am not good enough / I am a failure'.
target_behavior.function: Through self-pressure and self-blame, gains a sense of control or avoids the shame of being judged.
target_behavior.consequence: Frustration and Increased stress, diminished enjoyment of skateboarding, weakened motivation, Tense relationships with friends.

target_behavior.behavior: Setting unrealistic goals and excessively forcing myself to train
antecedent: Realizing I have not yet reached professional level
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by 'should' sentence patterns and an either-or view of achievement, regarding professionalization as the only valid standard.
target_behavior.function: Trying to quickly prove self-worth, Gaining recognition and a sense of control.
target_behavior.consequence: Worsened frustration, Rising stress, persistence and Reduced sense of enjoyment.
